features.summary: Dentries inside a dirfrag are ordered by name hash, and readdir returns them in that order.
features.description: CDir::items is keyed by dentry_key_t ordered by ceph_frag_value(hash) (24 bits), then name (byte compare), then snapid; readdir emits entries in this order from lower_bound of the resume key, skipping keys <= (offset_hash, offset name). With CEPH_READDIR_REPLY_BITFLAGS the MDS sets CEPH_READDIR_HASH_ORDER | CEPH_READDIR_OFFSET_HASH; the kernel recomputes each entry's hash to build f_pos (HASH_ORDER flag | hash24 << 28 | collision index), numbering same-hash entries in arrival order, so entries must arrive in non-decreasing 24-bit hash order (an entry below the current position makes ceph_readdir return EIO) and the name order within one hash keeps path2 resumption exact. On-disk omap keys (name_head, `name_<snap hex>`) are lexicographic, independent of this order. Names are compared byte-wise; the MDS performs no case folding or normalization.
features.notes: See also F-NS-032, F-NS-033.

legacy_parts.note: Readdir requests without CEPH_READDIR_REPLY_BITFLAGS: the MDS picks the frag without offset_hash, clears offset_str and sets neither CEPH_READDIR_HASH_ORDER nor CEPH_READDIR_OFFSET_HASH in the reply. Only kernels before v4.7 (kernel commit 956d39d631db) send readdir requests without CEPH_READDIR_REPLY_BITFLAGS. The 7.3 kernel sets the flag on every readdir and snapdir-listing request, and current libcephfs sets it on every readdir.

features.group: Fragment identity, name hashing and client exposure
features.name: Readdir fragment mapping and resume across refragmentation
features.summary: Fragment-tree side of readdir resume across splits and merges.
features.description: See F-NS-033. Fragment-side facts: readdir rdlocks the directory's filelock and dirfragtreelock; a frag that is no longer a leaf is mapped through the current dirfragtree (dirfragtree[offset_hash] or dirfragtree[frag value]), and the reply names the leaf it served, so positions keyed by name hash survive refragmentation.
features.notes: Ganesha's use of the offsets as cookies was not inspected (unverified).

features.group: Fragment identity, name hashing and client exposure
features.name: DirStat delegation hints
features.summary: Per-fragment authority and replica hints in replies that clients use to route requests.
features.description: Every trace dentry and every readdir reply carries DirStat {frag, auth = dir_auth.first (-1 = same as the directory inode's auth), dist = replica ranks plus self}; dist is filled only when this rank is auth, the dirfrag has replicas and mds_forward_all_requests_to_auth is false, and reflects actual replica holders. Encoded ENCODE_START(1, 1) for sessions with CEPHFS_FEATURE_REPLY_ENCODING, else as raw ceph_mds_reply_dirfrag {frag, auth, ndist, dist[]}. The kernel stores mds and up to 4 dist ranks per frag (dropping the record when ndist == 0 and auth equals the inode's auth) and sends USE_ANY_MDS requests to a random dist rank; libcephfs records fragmap[frag] = auth (negative erases), accepts dist only from the auth rank's replies and forces the frag to a leaf. Any rank can therefore receive any request and must serve it from replicas or forward. Hot-directory replication (dir_rep REP_ALL, MDirUpdate) is decided by the balancer ([balancer and pinning](../cpp-map/08-multi-mds/balancer-and-pinning.md)).
features.notes: See also F-PROTO-083 (DirStat encoding), F-PROTO-075 (client rank selection), F-MULTI-050.

legacy_parts.note: The raw ceph_mds_reply_dirfrag DirStat form (frag, auth, ndist, dist[] without an envelope) for sessions without CephFS bit 9. Only sessions without CephFS bit 9 (kernels up to v5.0, Ceph 13.2.x and older) get the raw form. The 7.3 kernel and current libcephfs advertise bit 9 and get the ENCODE_START(1, 1) form.

features.group: Fragment identity, name hashing and client exposure
features.name: Per-dirfrag size limit (ENOSPC)
features.summary: Creates fail with ENOSPC when the target dirfrag holds too many entries.
features.description: Server::check_fragment_space returns -ENOSPC when the target dirfrag's projected fragstat.size() (nfiles + nsubdirs, head entries only) is >= mds_bal_fragment_size_max (100000) for openc, mknod, mkdir, symlink, link and every rename that is not a link merge (including same-directory renames and renames over an existing name), and for the current stray dirfrag in prepare_stray_dentry, so unlink, rmdir and rename-over fail with ENOSPC when that stray frag is full (replayed requests excepted). The root directory is never fragmented, so / is limited to that many entries. CDir keeps num_head_items, num_head_null, num_snap_items and num_snap_null (asserted to sum to the item count) and num_dirty.
features.notes: Result frags of a split cannot be split again until the fragment op finishes, so very fast creates can push one toward the limit in that window (qa test_fragment). Exact per frag. See also F-NS-020 (gates in the request path), F-BG-004 (stray dirfrag), F-CACHE-082 (split thresholds).

features.group: Fragment identity, name hashing and client exposure
features.name: Per-directory entry limit
features.summary: An optional cap on the total entries of one directory.
features.description: With mds_dir_max_entries > 0 (default 0 = off, runtime option), Server::check_dir_max_entries returns ENOSPC for openc, mknod, mkdir, symlink, link and rename when the target directory's projected dirstat.nfiles + nsubdirs (remote dentries included) is at or above the limit, independently of fragmentation; the stray directory is not checked.
features.notes: Approximate across ranks: when the directory's dirfrags are on ranks other than the inode's auth, the inode dirstat is only as fresh as the last filelock gather, so creates on those ranks can exceed the limit (derived). For kclient async creates the ENOSPC would arrive after the client already reported success (leases-lock-caches-and-async-dirops). See also F-NS-020.

features.name: Size-triggered split and split checks
features.summary: Splitting a dirfrag that grows past a size threshold, re-checked after creates and on every dirfrag hit.
features.description: MDBalancer::maybe_fragment runs right after openc, mknod, mkdir, symlink, link and rename journal_and_reply, from every hit_dir (lookups, getattr, open, unlink/link/rename finish, dirfrag fetch and commit, readdir), at the end of a directory scrub and at the end of each fragment op. If should_split (split size > 0 and projected fragstat.size + num_snap_items > mds_bal_split_size, 10000), queue_split(dir, false) arms a timer of mds_bal_fragment_interval (5 s) once per frag (split_pending); the split is by mds_bal_split_bits (3, i.e. 8 children). maybe_fragment acts only if mds_bal_fragment_dirs is true and the interval > 0, the dirfrag is auth, and the inode is neither a base inode nor a stray directory; the callback drops the request if the rank is stopping or the frag is no longer cached or auth.

features.name: Fast split
features.summary: Splitting immediately when a dirfrag far exceeds the split size while a split is already pending.
features.description: If a split is already pending and should_split_fast holds (limit = mds_bal_split_size x mds_bal_fragment_fast_factor (1.5): projected fragstat size > limit, or, when size + head null dentries exceed the limit, the count of cached dentries whose projected linkage is non-null exceeds it), queue_split(dir, true) queues an immediate waiter that runs after the current dispatch instead of waiting for the timer.

features.name: Temperature-triggered split
features.summary: Splitting a busy dirfrag regardless of its size.
features.description: hit_dir increments decaying per-dirfrag popularity counters (half-life mds_decay_halflife, 5 s); an IRD count (inode reads: lookup, getattr, open) above mds_bal_split_rd (25000) or an IWR count above mds_bal_split_wr (10000) queues a split regardless of size. READDIR hits do not count toward mds_bal_split_rd (the documentation says they do).
features.notes: There is no size floor for temperature splits and merges look only at size, so a hot small directory can be split and later merged again (inference from the trigger code).

features.name: Size-triggered merge
features.summary: Merging small sibling dirfrags back together.
features.description: should_merge: not the root frag, fragstat.size + num_snap_items < mds_bal_merge_size (50), and not shallower than the ephemeral distributed-pin minimum. queue_merge arms a timer once per frag (merge_pending); the callback climbs toward the root while all dirfrags under the sibling are cached, auth and should_merge, then merges to the highest qualifying ancestor. merge_dir requires every frag under the target to be cached and the target not to be a leaf; its bits value is computed from the first source only (sign significant, magnitude informational).

features.name: Fragmentation preconditions and exclusions
features.summary: Directories and situations in which no split or merge happens.
features.description: can_fragment silently drops the operation when the file system is read-only, the cluster is degraded (any rank failed, damaged or in replay..clientreplay), the directory's parent is a stray directory, the inode is ~mdsN or /.ceph, the inode is quiesced, the inode is the root directory (added by commit f4bcf5bfd53, 2025), or any source dirfrag is being scrubbed, already FRAGMENTING, not auth, BADFRAG, or freezing/frozen (dir or tree). split_dir drops splits that would exceed 24 bits. maybe_fragment also skips base inodes and stray directories (strays are pre-fragmented by stray rotation, [strays and purge](../cpp-map/11-background-services/strays-and-purge.md)).
features.notes: See also F-ADM-052 (dirfrag split/merge commands).

legacy_parts.note: The /.ceph (ino 2, CEPH_INO_CEPH) exclusion in can_fragment. Ino 2 exists only on file systems created by C++ releases before v0.79, because commit 81bcf43080a (2014) stopped creating /.ceph and left it on existing file systems. No component at this commit creates ino 2.

features.name: Fragment operation (FRAGMENTDIR)
features.summary: The internal request that freezes source dirfrags, refragments the cache and makes the change durable.
features.description: split_dir / merge_dir create an internal MDRequest CEPH_MDS_OP_FRAGMENTDIR (0x01500) and a fragments[base] entry (at most one per base dirfrag). Steps: freeze each source (auth pin, STATE_FRAGMENTING, freeze_dir; a mixed set of subtree roots is made homogeneous with aux subtrees); mark and complete (full fetch of incomplete sources, commit a never-committed root frag first, wait CREATED for a root frag still being created, pin every dentry with PIN_FRAGMENTING, set STATE_DNPINNEDFRAG, register WAIT_FROZEN and flush the journal so in-flight requests' auth pins become journal-safe and drop); when all are frozen, take the dirfragtreelock wrlock plus filelock/nestlock scatter-gather pins with nonblocking auth pins (a quiescelock wrlock is added); journal EFragment PREPARE (original frags with rollback fnodes, new dirlumps, inode fullbit if inode auth else DIRTYDFT) and refragment the cache; when safe, write the new objects; then send replica notifies, journal COMMIT, unfreeze the new frags and drop locks (keeping the dirfragtreelock while notify acks are pending); after COMMIT is safe purge old objects and journal FINISH; finally clear FRAGMENTING and re-evaluate the result frags. Result frags keep FRAGMENTING and an auth pin until FINISH and all acks, so they cannot be refragmented or frozen for export meanwhile.
features.notes: COMMIT and FINISH are submitted without an explicit journal flush. Code-reading findings: the quiesce-overdrive abort can call request_finish twice (visible as a double count of mds_cache.ireq_fragmentdir); a RADOS error storing a new frag goes to handle_write_error and leaves the op stuck with its new frags frozen. Dev option mds_kill_dirfrag_at provides kill points 1..10 for tests. EFragment encoding: [events and replay](../cpp-map/06-journal/events-and-replay.md).

features.name: Dentry repartitioning and stat-delta preservation
features.summary: Moving dentries between dirfrag objects in memory while keeping directory statistics exact.
features.description: CDir::split creates 2^bits children that copy the replica map, dir_auth, freeze_tree_state, MASK_STATE_FRAGMENT_KEPT | COMPLETE state and popularity scaled by 1/2^bits; every dentry moves to the child chosen by the updated tree, and dentry waiters are re-homed by name hash. CDir::merge takes dir_auth and freeze state from the first sub (all must match), the maximum nonce per replica, the union of kept state and the highest fnode version; popularity of the merged frag starts at zero. steal_dentry moves the CDentry object itself (state, locks, client leases, replicas, pins) and recomputes counters, fragstat from linkage, rstat from children's accounted_rstat, num_inodes_with_caps (moving the open-file-table registration), dirty lists and nested auth pins. Pending deltas (fragstat - accounted_fragstat, rstat - accounted_rstat) go to the first child on split and are summed on merge, so the next scatter-gather still propagates them. Dentry leases survive because objects are moved, not recreated.

features.name: New dirfrag object write and old object purge
features.summary: Cache side of writing new dirfrag objects and purging old ones in a split or merge.
features.description: See F-STORE-034 for the object operations and their order. Cache-side facts: after PREPARE is safe each result frag is marked dirty and new and committed with ignore_authpinnability; because it is FRAGMENTING and new, _omap_commit writes every non-null dentry without the stat guard, chunked by mds_dir_max_commit_size with the header last (encoding on the finisher thread without mds_lock). Between the store and the purge, dentries exist in both old and new objects; cephfs-data-scan scan_links tolerates such duplicates.

features.name: Replica notification of refragmentation
features.summary: Telling ranks that replicate a directory's dirfrags about a split or merge.
features.description: After the new objects are stored, MMDSFragmentNotify (0x209; base dirfrag, int8 bits, replica-dir blobs of the result frags, ack_wanted (v2); header tid = request tid) goes to each replica rank of the first result frag that is in REJOIN or later and not still in rejoin_gather. Replicas (the message is dropped before REJOIN; a missing directory inode aborts the daemon, which trim_inode prevents by keeping replica directory inodes whose dirfragtreelock is unreadable) refragment without freezing, decode the replica dirs and reply MMDSFragmentNotifyAck (0x212) if asked. ack_wanted is set only when the first result frag is a subtree root, this rank is not the inode auth and the replica is not the inode auth; the dirfragtreelock wrlock is held until all acks arrive or the ranks fail. Cache expiries naming old frags are dropped, dentry expiries are re-routed by hash, and discover replies correct the base frag.
features.notes: Ranks before REJOIN miss notifies and learn the fragmentation from rejoin. Acks are ignored while the auth is not active.

features.name: Fragtree propagation through dirfragtreelock
features.summary: Letting a rank that owns some dirfrags, but not the directory inode, change the fragment tree.
features.description: A rank that is auth for a dirfrag but not for the directory inode fragments it while holding the IDFT scatterlock wrlock in LOCK_MIX (requested from the inode auth with REQSCATTER); it journals DIRTYDFT dirlumps and marks the lock dirty. Its lock payload carries a dirty flag, the tree and the frags it is auth for; the inode auth forces those frags to leaves in its tree and marks the lock dirty, so scatter writebehind journals and stores the updated tree; replicas accept the auth's tree while forcing their open frags to stay leaves and clear STATE_DIRTYDFT. A log segment with dirty dirfragtree state cannot expire until scatter_nudge flushes it; rejoin messages carry the dft lock state. Lock state machine: [lock types and state machines](../cpp-map/05-locking/lock-types-and-state-machines.md).

features.name: Subtree map maintenance on split and merge
features.summary: Keeping delegation points correct when subtree-root dirfrags are split or merged.
features.description: adjust_dir_fragments edits the subtree map directly: splitting a subtree root makes every child a subtree root that replaces the source in its parent's bound set, and the source's bounds go to the child that now contains each; merging requires the sources to be all subtree roots or none (asserted), unions their bounds and replaces them with the merged frag. AUXSUBTREE, EXPORTBOUND and IMPORTBOUND survive split and merge.

features.name: Abort, requeue and cancellation of fragment operations
features.summary: How fragment operations back off to avoid deadlocks and what happens to them on failures.
features.description: Lock acquisition aborts the op and re-queues it (delayed split or merge) when a nonblocking auth pin would block (for example the parent dirfrag is freezing for export or fragmentation), a remote auth-pin reply carries an error, or the directory's quiescelock cannot be wrlocked (would deadlock with quiesce_inode ops on children). A quiesce_inode or quiesce_path op that meets a FRAGMENTING dir aborts the op asynchronously through the same path unless all its dirs are already frozen. Stale-freeze cancellation and cancellation of ops before PREPARE on another rank's failure unfreeze without re-queue; ops past PREPARE just drop the failed rank from the ack wait. A later maybe_fragment re-arms dropped ops.
features.notes: See also F-QOS-048 (quiesce and fragmentation).

features.name: Recovery of in-flight fragment operations
features.summary: Rolling interrupted splits and merges forward or back after a crash.
features.description: EFragment (event type 6; op PREPARE 1, COMMIT 2, ROLLBACK 3, FINISH 4; ino, basefrag, signed bits, metablob, orig_frags, rollback fnodes; ENCODE_START(5, 4)) replay maintains uncommitted_fragments: PREPARE adds an entry (and refragments the cache if the inode is cached), COMMIT marks it committed, FINISH erases it. When the rank leaves replay (resolve_start, or reconnect_start for single-rank recovery), rollback_uncommitted_fragments deletes the old objects and journals FINISH for committed ops; PREPARE-only ops journal ROLLBACK (original frags restored from the rollback fnodes and marked dirty), then delete the new objects and journal FINISH, without waiting for ROLLBACK to be safe. A segment containing a PREPARE cannot expire before FINISH, and rejoin_done waits for all uncommitted fragments. Safety rests on: new objects complete before COMMIT is journaled, old objects removed only after COMMIT is durable, and COMMIT journaled before any mutation of the new frags.
features.notes: mds.dir_split / mds.dir_merge are incremented when the purge completes, including for rolled-back ops. See also F-STORE-034 (EFragment record and object cleanup).

features.name: Forced refragmentation during replay, resolve and rejoin
features.summary: Making the cache's dirfrags match what the journal or peers describe.
features.description: Every replayed EMetaBlob dirlump forces the cache to hold exactly that dirfrag (get_force_dirfrag -> force_dir_fragment: return it if open, else split the nearest open ancestor, else merge what is open under it); replayed inode fullbits replace the fragtree and force_dirfrags refragments open dirfrags to match; ESubtreeMap replay forces bound frags. Resolve forces local dirfrags to match peers' subtree claims (get_force_dirfrag_bound_set only splits, never merges); rejoin acks carry strong dirfrags that refragment replicas; a strong rejoin naming non-leaf frags is mapped onto local leaves and its dentries re-picked by name hash.

features.name: Migration and fragmentation mutual exclusion
features.summary: Keeping subtree export and dirfrag split/merge from interleaving on the same directories.
features.description: An export rdlocks the dirfragtreelock of the exported dirfrag's inode and of every bound inode (scatterlock state shipped for bounds would be useless if a refragment raced); can_fragment refuses freezing or frozen trees; a fragment op's auth pins block an export's tree freeze; maybe_split_export skips dirfrags freezing or frozen as dirs; the importer forces each imported dirfrag to be a leaf of its tree. Export protocol: [subtree migration](../cpp-map/08-multi-mds/subtree-migration.md).

features.name: Effects of a fragment freeze on clients
features.summary: Stalls and cap changes clients observe while a dirfrag is being split or merged.
features.description: From freeze until the new objects are stored: operations needing auth pins in the dirfrag wait, including those on child inodes (CInode::can_auth_pin defers to the parent dirfrag) and, on the dirfrag auth, lookups and getattrs that rdlock a dentry there (acquire_locks auth-pins every auth object it rdlocks); the traversal itself does not wait. Cap messages for child inodes are deferred while the parent dirfrag is frozen, or freezing and the inode has no auth pins (unless a lock cache pins the dirfrag); max_size increases and cap reissue wait for unfreeze. freeze_dir invalidates lock caches that pin the dirfrag, revoking DIR_CREATE / DIR_UNLINK so clients fall back to synchronous creates and unlinks. Readdir and snapshot lookup-by-hash on any frag of the directory wait while the dirfragtreelock wrlock is held. Replica ranks never freeze their copies. Lock caches: [leases, lock caches and async dirops](../cpp-map/02-client-protocol/leases-lock-caches-and-async-dirops.md).
